records.title: Nahrungsmittelinhaltsstoffe strukturbezogen einordnen
records.description: Die lernende Person kann ausgewählte Inhaltsstoffe von Nahrungsmitteln anhand ihres submikroskopischen Baus vergleichen, Makro- und Mikronährstoffen zuordnen und ihre Bedeutung für den menschlichen Körper beschreiben.

records.chatGptNotes: Fresh current V3-A: original1672x941 and actual Chromium360/680 inspected. Three linked generic sugar units, a three-tail fat symbol, a folded bead-chain protein symbol and positive/negative mineral-ion icons are differentiated correctly as broad groups. Food arrows refer to a food mixture, not a claim that a depicted food contains only one constituent. These are class icons rather than literal atom/valence or salt-formula drawings. The fat symbol has three fatty-acid tails and is not a one- or two-tail phospholipid formula. The three ion symbols do not specify a stoichiometric salt unit. Supports comparing broad submicroscopic structural motifs and mineral micronutrient versus major organic nutrient classes. At 360 px all four groups, labels and distinct motifs are recognizable; at 680 px chain/tail/ion details are clear. No essential tiny paragraph text. The bound current goal has no primary resource; this reviewed existing PNG adds an available image without a new chemical body. Front-facing food and class icons; no person/tool/paper viewpoint contradiction. No Human Approval, full-goal assessment, source closure or new native D review.

records.title: Nukleinsäuren als Biomoleküle einordnen
records.description: Die lernende Person kann Nukleinsäuren anhand grundlegender Strukturmerkmale als Biomoleküle einordnen und ihre biologische Funktion im Vergleich zu Fetten, Kohlenhydraten und Proteinen beschreiben.
records.subject: chemie
records.chatGptNotes: Fresh current V3-A: original1672x941 and actual Chromium360/680 inspected. Actual old JPG contains G-T and A-C pairings. The existing PNG shows A-T, G-C, T-A and C-G; the nucleotide icon connects phosphate to sugar to base and the ladder has repeating sugar/phosphate sides plus an information symbol. It is explicitly a schematic Baustein/ladder model: base polygons are not heterocyclic atom formulas, and the repeated two dotted connector rows per pair are generic pairing connectors, not a quantitative hydrogen-bond model. In particular the picture must not be used to teach two hydrogen bonds for G-C: actual Watson-Crick A-T has two and G-C three. No such count claim or atom assignment appears in the supplied image/alt text. Supports basic nucleic-acid structure and information function. It is a DNA example of the nucleic-acid class, not a depiction of all RNA forms, antiparallel end chemistry or all comparisons with fats/proteins/carbohydrates. Those whole-goal teaching/assessment duties remain separate. All four base-letter pairs, DNA label, nucleotide group and information cue remain distinct at 360 px; the small Zucker word is supporting detail. At 680 px even supporting wording is legible. Reuses an already generated correction PNG for the evidenced wrong-base-pair problem. No fresh generation or mandatory cosmetic redesign. Flat explanatory ladder, not a literal helix or an atom model. The information-book label faces the viewer and is not reversed relative to a person. No Human Approval, full-goal assessment, source closure or new native D review.

records.title: Nahrungsbestandteile nach Polarität und Resorption einordnen
records.description: Die lernende Person kann Nahrungsbestandteile als hydrophil, lipophil oder amphiphil einordnen und damit Vitaminresorption, Verweildauer im Körper sowie geeignete Lösemittel bei der Lebensmittelzubereitung begründen.
records.subject: chemie
records.chatGptNotes: Fresh current V3-A: original1672x941 and actual Chromium360/680 inspected. Hydrophilic blue and lipophilic orange examples are separated; amphiphile blue heads face the aqueous blue region and orange tails face the oil region. The circular aggregate has water-facing heads and inward unpolar tails. The intestine label explicitly says Dünndarm, not stomach. Schematic phase and aggregate cartoons, no individual molecule formula, atom count or detailed membrane-transport mechanism. The enlargement illustrates a micellar lumen environment; it does not show intact micelles traversing intestinal epithelium or replacing all vitamin-specific uptake routes. Supports polarity, phase compatibility and a micellar intestinal-resorption example. It makes no blanket water-soluble=no-storage claim. Water-soluble B12 is a relevant counterexample: substantial body storage and intrinsic-factor-dependent distal-ileal uptake mean polarity alone cannot determine residence time or resorption mechanism. Solvent choice, individual vitamin transport and residence-time limits remain part of the whole goal/profile, not newly waived. The three class labels, phase orientation, inward micelle tails and Dünndarm remain recognizable at 360 px, with ample contrast and no essential fine text; 680 px is clear throughout. The actual old JPG places a bile/micelle label with a stomach drawing and groups B vitamins with short-storage wording. The new existing PNG uses a Dünndarm model and removes that universal storage statement. No student/paper viewpoint. The magnification link is conventional schematic anatomy rather than a claim of histological scale or direct whole-micelle blood entry. No Human Approval, full-goal assessment, source closure or new native D review.
